AIAA 3201 · Project 3 · Direction B

Global Metric Scale Calibration

Method

We calibrate the metric depth predicted by a frozen UniDepthV2 ViT-S/14 model with a single positive scale factor. The model receives only RGB at inference. For each of the 795 NYUv2 development images, we compute the median of the ground-truth-to-prediction ratios over valid pixels. We then take the median of these image-level estimates, giving each development image equal influence in the second median.

si = medianp ∈ Ωi [digt(p) / d̂i(p)],   s = mediani ∈ dev(si),   d̂cal(p) = s · d̂(p).

We use 480 × 640 depth maps and the Eigen crop (rows 45–470 and columns 41–600, zero-indexed). The fit uses finite, positive predictions and finite ground truth strictly between 0.001 and 10 m. The resulting scale, 0.9340532609, is fixed for all 654 held-out images. Both test conditions use the same crop and ground-truth mask. Predictions are clipped to [0.001, 10] m after the optional scaling. Test ground truth is used only to compute metrics, which are averaged over images.

Results on NYUv2

MethodAbsRel ↓RMSE (m) ↓δ1 (%) ↑
UniDepthV2, uncalibrated0.1294250.42372987.5653
UniDepthV2, calibrated0.1030030.38802490.0662

The global calibration reduces AbsRel by 20.4% and RMSE by 8.4%, while improving δ1 by 2.50 percentage points. AbsRel decreases on 457 of 654 test images and increases on 197. The factor corrects a systematic scale bias in this split while preserving the spatial structure of the prediction. Images whose original depths are already too small can degrade after scaling.

Qualitative comparison

Inference used FP32 with UniDepthV2 resolution level 9 on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. Sources include NYU Depth V2 and UniDepthV2.
